title: Incremental event hydration worker for console analytics catch-up
creator: Miles Chen
description: Build an incremental event hydration worker that can perform efficient, idempotent catch-up of Console usage events into the analytics pipeline. This worker fills gaps caused by transient ingestion failures, late arrivals from edge collectors, and small schema-mismatches without requiring a full historical reprocess. Goal: reduce cost and time-to-consistency for typical catch-up windows (hours to days) and provide a safe operator experience for larger backfills.
acceptance_criteria: Worker can claim and process time-windowed leases without duplicate processing (idempotency verified via event_hash).
Ability to catch up 7 days of missed events in < 6 hours for a single region (on our staging size cluster).
Metrics exposed: processed_events_total, dedupe_rate, late_event_ratio, avg_processing_latency, lease_conflicts_total.
Produces output compatible with existing BigQuery/warehouse schema and tagging required by Console dashboards.
Automated integration tests that simulate duplicate events, schema evolution, and partial failures.
Runbook updated with steps to pause/advance leases and to promote to a full reprocess when needed.
tasks: Design lease format and storage (DynamoDB with partitioned checkpoints + optimistic lease TTL).
Implement worker core: stream read -> transform -> dedupe -> write to staging topic/warehouse sink.
Add idempotency layer using event_hash + write-through cache to avoid double-writes to warehouse.
Instrumentation: Prometheus metrics, structured logs, trace spans; push dashboards for canary run.
Integration tests: local harness + staging cluster test that replays golden fixtures.
Docs: Confluence runbook + operator docs + example CLI to advance/inspect leases.
Run canary on one customer sandbox and validate dashboards for 48 hours before regional rollout.
risks: Lease storming under heavy historical windows could overload ingestion topic; mitigation: window fanout and backpressure tokens.
Schema drift causing silent drops; mitigation: strict schema validation + dead-letter topic for malformed events.
Cost of catch-up for multi-day windows could be high if naive; mitigation: incremental checkpoints and sampling-based cost estimate before run.
Edge-case duplicates across original ingestion and hydration path; mitigation: global event_hash and canonical dedupe window.

comments: 2026-02-19: Spike complete. Verified that DynamoDB leases + small worker pool can scale to staging replay rates. - Miles

2026-03-07: Performance test: 12-hour window processed in 3.8 hours on staging 4x-worker config. Observed ~3.5% duplicate candidates that were deduped client-side. Good baseline but need to tune batch sizes. - Aditi
